title: Observationally indistinguishable space-times
version: in Foundations of Space-Time Theories, Minnesota Studies in the Philosophy of Science 8, Univ. of Minnesota Press, 1977, pp. 61-80
locator: definition of observational indistinguishability and the 'causally bizarre' conjecture, read via Manchak 2009's quoted text and Norton 2009
relevance: Shows generically that pointwise-isometric pasts never fix the global spacetime; the causally bizarre class (I^-(p)=M) is the strongest 'past sees everything' version.
limits: Original chapter not read this session; page range from Manchak 2009's reference.

title: Is Prediction Possible in General Relativity?
conclusion: Author's claims: predicting one's own future is possible only in a closed universe (compact slice); under his more adequate definition prediction is essentially impossible in GR.
proof_status: Theorem not checked at source; repo paper cites its p. 319 theorem.
relevance: Fixes the exception class for the monadic principle: compact slices only.
limits: Body text not read; abstract-level this session.

title: Can we know the global structure of spacetime?
version: Studies in History and Philosophy of Modern Physics 40 (2009) 53-56, doi:10.1016/j.shpsb.2008.07.004
locator: abstract, the observational-indistinguishability definition, the 'causally bizarre' definition and Malament's conjecture read via page extraction (~2 pages of text)
assumptions: Classical GR; I^-(p) isometric pointwise between spacetimes.
conclusion: Settles and strengthens Malament's 1977 conjecture: global structure of every cosmological model is underdetermined in a robust sense.
relevance: Strongest generic negative against 'every event's past determines the spacetime'.
limits: Extraction partial; proofs and the exact strengthening statement not read.

title: The Inductive Significance of Observationally Indistinguishable Spacetimes
conclusion: Author's claim: 'a specification of the observable past always fails to fix the remainder of a spacetime'; credits Glymour (1977) and Malament (1977) for the underlying results.
relevance: Confirms the exact negative formulation of the monadic condition in the literature and locates Glymour 1977.
limits: Abstract-level only; Glymour 1977 reached only through it.

title: Electromagnetism and time-asymmetry
locator: arXiv abstract fetched this session; full text previously read by the horizons/massive-minkowski lane (record mm-weinstein-2011)
assumptions: Classical Maxwell theory; observer limited to past light cone.
conclusion: Author's claim: prediction needs the added assumption that all fields have sources in their past (no incoming radiation, Sommerfeld condition); hence 'a lawlike time-asymmetry'.
proof_status: Argument, no theorem (per sibling lane's full-text record).
relevance: Nearest predecessor for the law-promotion move; the monadic principle universalizes its assumption over all events.
limits: My own read is abstract-level; full-text claims inherited from the sibling lane's record.
